The storyboard sheet itself is never visible: no multi-panel grid, split screen, panel borders, divider lines, gutters, white margins, page edges, cropped fragments from adjacent panels, captions, labels, timestamps, or typography.

launcherMechanics: Launcher housings have no bit-beast emblem; emblems belong only on top center chips. Classic ripcord-launcher attachment lock: before a pull, insert both close-set launcher posts fully into the paired launcher slots immediately beside the central Bit Chip/center gap, one slot on each side of the central axis and never on the outer Attack Ring or Weight Disk and rotate the top in its spin-compatible locking direction until both posts are retained. The top must sit level and flush beneath the launcher with no visible gap, tilt, dangling, floating or single-post support; its tip points straight down. The rigid toothed ripcord is fully inserted through the gear housing. One hand holds the launcher steady while the other pulls the ring once. The top stays locked during gear acceleration, then both posts disengage at the release event and the top descends under gravity tip-first. After release, the launcher underside is empty and the fully extracted ripcord is separate in the pulling hand.

continuity_handoff.outgoing: All three crouch ready at fixed positions; one top firmly twist-locked level and flush below each launcher on both posts; short ripcords inserted, fingers hooked through rings; bowl empty.

launcherCenterSlotGeometryLock: Launcher center-slot geometry lock: the launcher has exactly two short, close-set engagement prongs symmetric about its central axis. Both prongs enter the paired launcher slots immediately beside the Beyblade's central Bit Chip/center gap, one on each side of the axis. They never attach to the outer Attack Ring, Weight Disk, perimeter, or tip. Before release the top is level, flush, and firmly retained on both prongs; at release both prongs disengage together and the top becomes fully unsupported, descending tip-first under gravity.
beybladeDynamicsLock: Observable Beyblade dynamics lock: every active top is a rigid palm-sized gyroscope with one tip in continuous contact with the stadium after landing. High RPM produces rapid circumferential texture blur around the Attack Ring; center emblems may remain centered but perimeter markings may not stay crisp or frozen. The contact tip and center of mass define one coherent axis; the top never hovers. Any tilt produces continuous gyroscopic precession: the lean direction rotates around the contact point and may damp toward vertical at high RPM or widen as RPM falls, but it never freezes at one lean angle or compass direction. Tip friction, gravity, and the bowl tangent create a continuous curved trajectory with position continuous from frame to frame; tops do not hold a staged side-by-side formation, teleport, or pivot on a glued point. Each collision is a brief Attack-Ring-to-Attack-Ring impulse followed immediately by visible separation, tangential deflection or rebound, changed travel velocity, wobble, and some speed loss; tops never overlap, stick together, or cluster like magnets. Mechanical energy then decreases monotonically through friction and impacts: orbit speed and RPM decay, precession widens, the rim or base may scrape, and a fully stopped unsupported top falls onto its side. Preserve every owner's authored top design, axial spin direction, path, and outcome across cuts.
launcherAttachmentProximityLock: Launcher-to-Beyblade proximity lock: whenever a Beyblade is loaded before release, its flat upper face is in direct visible contact with the launcher underside, with zero visible air gap. Exactly two short close-set launcher prongs are fully inserted into the paired slots beside the central Bit Chip and twist-locked together; the top is level, centered on the launcher axis, and its tip points straight down. The launcher and loaded top move as one rigid assembly with identical position and tilt: no dangling top, long connector, exposed suspension gap, single-post support, floating, or early separation. The visible gap begins only on the single release frame, when both prongs disengage together and the already-spinning top immediately descends tip-first under gravity.
multiTopReferenceLayoutLock: The multi-top reference image supplies design and owner identity only. Never reproduce its side-by-side catalogue layout, common pose, common lean, or spacing in the stadium; render each top as a separate physical object at its authored position, spin phase, tilt phase, velocity, and trajectory.
rotationalCausalityLock: Rotational-causality lock: spin energy comes from the ripcord-driven launcher gear while the top is still mechanically engaged. Before the pull the loaded top is stationary. During the pull it accelerates while remaining flush-mounted; on every successful release, the very first unsupported airborne frame already shows rapid high-RPM axial rotation and strong circumferential Attack Ring blur. The top carries that same continuous rotation through tip-first landing, with no stopped, crisp, or low-RPM airborne or landed interval followed by a later spin-up. After detachment its RPM may persist briefly, transfer through a visible rim impact, or decrease through drag, friction, scraping and collision, but it never increases or restarts without a photographed external torque. An explicitly failed release that receives no usable launcher torque remains non-spinning, falls under gravity, and never starts spinning by itself.
launcherNoConnectorLock: Launcher silhouette lock: the Beyblade's upper face sits immediately beneath and touches the actual launcher housing. Only the two very short engagement prongs hidden inside the top's center slots may connect them. Never draw any long black rod, vertical shaft, stem, axle, neck, cable, string, spacer, tether, suspension bar, or extended post between launcher and Beyblade.
